statement.p: The path C is a line segment of length 5 in the plane starting at (5,2). For f(x,y) = 3 x + 4 y, consider \int_C \nabla f \cdot d\vec r.
(a) Where should the other end of the line segment C be placed to maximize the value of the integral?
(b) What is the maximum value of the integral?

static.solution:
(a) To maximize the line integral, we choose C to be parallel to 
abla f= 3\vec i + 4\vec j. Thus C has parametric equation \vec r= (5\vec i+ 2\vec j) + t\vec v where \vec v= 3\vec i + 4\vec j, so x = 5 + 3 t \quad y= 2 + 4 t. If the other end of C is at (x_1,y_1), since the length of C is 5, we have \sqrt{(x_1 - 5)^2 + (y_1 - 2)^2} = 5, or \sqrt{(3 t)^2+(4 t)^2} = 5, so t\,\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = t\cdot 5 = 5. Thus t = 1 at (x_1,y_1), so x_1 = 5 + 1\cdot 3 = 8\quad\hbox{ and }\quad y_1 = 2 + 1\cdot 4 = 6, and C ends at the point (8,6).
(b) By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals, \int_C 
abla f \cdot d\vec r = f(8,6) - f(5,2) =(3\cdot 8 + 4\cdot 6) - (3\cdot 5 + 4\cdot 2) = 25. Alternately, since 
abla f and C are parallel, \int_C 
abla f\cdot d\vec r = \Vert{
abla f}\Vert\cdot\hbox{Length of }C = 5 \cdot 5 = 25.
